title: Construction Safety Visual Screening Rules (English, R-CES subset)
description: Schema for data/rule/rule.json: the self-contained English rule library this benchmark conditions on, reduced to the fields the R-CES line consumes. Auxiliary normative fields used by other compliance pipelines are intentionally omitted from this projection.

rule_id.description: Stable rule identifier used by matched_rule_id. Do not rename without migrating annotations.

visual_checkpoints.description: Fields a VLM or human reviewer can inspect visually from a single image.

required_checkpoints.description: Materialized list of every visual_checkpoints key for this rule. MUST stay in sync with the keys of visual_checkpoints (same set, validated by validate_rces_pairs.py). Observation-layer fields observed_checkpoints / missing_checkpoints in the pair file may only reference values from this list.

critical_checkpoints.description: Subset of required_checkpoints that gate the single-image screening conclusion: if any of these cannot be observed, the image alone cannot yield a screening verdict and the pair should be abstained/undecidable. AI-proposed from visual_screening_rule; may be empty for requires_external_evidence rules whose undecidability comes from non_visual_fields rather than missing visual checkpoints.

critical_checkpoints_status.description: Provenance of critical_checkpoints: ai_proposed_needs_human_review before a human confirms the critical set, human_reviewed once confirmed.

non_visual_fields.description: Optional. Fields that bear on the rule but cannot be reliably decided from a single image (e.g. a material's identification label), so they are deliberately kept OUT of visual_checkpoints / required_checkpoints and need human/on-site or external evidence. Observation-layer checkpoint lists never reference these keys.

visual_screening_rule.description: Single-image risk screening expression using visible checkpoints only.

visual_retrieval_text.description: Encoder-facing scene-anchor text for image-rule similarity search and RAG-style candidate generation; it describes visible objects, components, PPE, protective elements, passages, openings, edges, equipment, and coarse visual states only, and is not a human label or compliance-decision field.
